articles.title: How Bluesky draws its logo on screenshots
articles.summary: Bluesky's logo appears on screenshots due to a clever use of a package called package expo-privacy-sensitive, which renders the button content into a UITextField and hides it by blanking the layer when taking a screenshot. This allows the logo to be visible in the screenshot, even when switching between apps. The package's isSecureTextEntry property is set to true, which enables this behavior. This trick is not unique to Bluesky, as other platforms like Telegram and Signal have also used similar techniques to hide their logos on screenshots.

articles.title: AI;DR (AI; Didn't Read)
articles.summary: AI;DR (AI; Didn't Read) is a solution for ignoring the walls of slop that developers often encounter with AI-generated content. The AI;DR acronym stands for "Ignore the Don't Read" and is a new approach to dealing with AI output that prioritizes human touch and understanding over technical accuracy. By ignoring AI-generated content, developers can focus on the actual content and message, rather than getting bogged down in the technical details. This approach is particularly useful in situations where 100% AI-generated content is expected, such as customer support or social media posts.

This solution uses the kexec mechanism to execute another kernel, replacing the running kernel without shutting down the server. The old kernel can still be accessed in RAM, but the new kernel can use a passphrase to decrypt the hard drive, saving several minutes of rebooting time. This approach retains the security of full-disk encryption while providing convenient and reliable reboots.
